lessons.title: Chess Basics
lessons.description: The board, the goal, and how a game is won. Start here.

steps.explanation: Chess is played on an 8x8 board. White moves first. The goal is to checkmate the enemy king — trap it so it cannot escape capture.
Always set up with a light square in the bottom-right corner. Each player starts with 16 pieces.

steps.prompt: Make your first move: push the e-pawn two squares (e4).
steps.explanation: 1.e4 is one of the best first moves — it grabs the center and opens lines for your bishop and queen. Big Brain Move.

lessons.title: How Pieces Move
lessons.description: Pawns, knights, bishops, rooks, queen and king — learn every move.

steps.explanation: Knights move in an L-shape: two squares one way, one square perpendicular. They are the only piece that can jump over others.
Nf3 is a perfect developing move — the knight controls central squares and eyes e5. Clean Move 🔥
Bishops move diagonally, rooks move in straight lines. The queen combines both. The king moves one square in any direction.

lessons.title: Opening Principles
lessons.description: The 3 golden rules that win more games than any opening theory.

steps.explanation: Pawns and pieces in the center control more squares and give your army room to breathe.

steps.prompt: Start with a central pawn move (e4).
steps.explanation: 1.e4 or 1.d4 both fight for the center. That's principle #1 done.
Rule 2: Develop knights and bishops quickly. Rule 3: Castle early to keep your king safe. Don't move the same piece twice in the opening.

lessons.title: Control the Center
lessons.description: Why the four central squares decide most games.

steps.explanation: A knight in the center controls up to 8 squares; in the corner only 2. Central control = more power and mobility.
1.e4 stakes a claim in the center and frees your bishop and queen. Big Brain Move.

steps.prompt: Support your center by developing: Nf3.
steps.explanation: 2.Nf3 develops a piece and adds pressure to the center. You Found It.

lessons.title: Develop Your Pieces
lessons.description: Get your army out fast — passive pieces lose games.

steps.explanation: Generally develop knights first (they have fewer good squares), then bishops, then castle.

steps.prompt: Develop a knight toward the center (Nf3).
steps.explanation: A developing move like Nf3 or Nc3 activates a piece and fights for the center. Time to Grind.

lessons.title: King Safety
lessons.description: Castle early and tuck your king behind a wall of pawns.

steps.explanation: Castling tucks the king into the corner and connects your rooks. Do it early — a king in the center is a target.
O-O moves the king to g1 and the rook to f1. Your king is safe and your rook is active. GG.

lessons.title: Tactical Thinking
lessons.description: Train your eye to spot forcing moves: checks, captures, threats.

steps.explanation: Before every move, scan for forcing moves. Forcing moves limit your opponent's replies and often win material.

steps.prompt: White to move — find the knight fork!
steps.explanation: Nf6+ forks the king and queen. After the king moves, Nxd5 wins the queen. Big Brain Move.

lessons.title: Forks
lessons.description: One piece, two targets. The knight's favorite trick.

steps.explanation: A fork attacks two (or more) pieces at once. Knights are the best forkers because their targets can't defend each other.
Nf6+ hits the king (check) and the queen. The king must move, then you grab the queen. You Found It.

lessons.title: Pins
lessons.description: Freeze a piece by attacking what's behind it.

steps.explanation: A pin attacks a piece that shields a more valuable piece behind it. The pinned piece can't move without exposing the one behind.

steps.prompt: Pin the c6 knight to the king (Bb5).
steps.explanation: Bb5 pins the c6 knight against the e8 king — the knight is frozen. This is the heart of the Ruy Lopez.

lessons.title: Skewers
lessons.description: A pin in reverse — hit the big piece first.

steps.explanation: A skewer attacks a valuable piece, forcing it to move and exposing a piece behind it. The opposite of a pin.

steps.prompt: Skewer the king to win the queen (Rh8+).
steps.explanation: Rh8+ checks the king; when it steps aside, Rxb8 wins the queen. Clean Move 🔥

lessons.title: Discovered Attacks
lessons.description: Move one piece, unleash another. Chess dynamite.

steps.explanation: Moving one piece uncovers an attack from a piece behind it. When the moving piece also attacks something, it's a double whammy.

steps.prompt: Unleash the bishop with a knight move that also hits the queen!
steps.explanation: Nf5+ discovers check from the b2 bishop AND attacks the d6 queen. The king must respond, then Nxd6 wins the queen.

lessons.title: Double Attacks
lessons.description: Two threats, one move. They can only stop one.

steps.explanation: A double attack creates two threats at once. Your opponent can only meet one — the other wins.

steps.prompt: Check the king and hit the rook in one move (Qe4+).
steps.explanation: Qe4+ gives check and attacks the h4 rook. After the king moves, Qxh4 wins the rook. Big Brain Move.

lessons.title: Checkmate Patterns
lessons.description: Learn the mating nets every player must know.

steps.explanation: A king trapped behind its own pawns is vulnerable to a rook or queen on the back rank. Always make luft (an escape square)!
Ra8# — the king is boxed in by its own pawns and can't escape. Checkmate. GG.

lessons.title: Endgames
lessons.description: Convert your advantage: promotion and basic mates.

steps.explanation: In the endgame, pawns become queens. A single passed pawn can decide the game — push it and promote.

steps.prompt: Promote your pawn to a queen (a8=Q).
steps.explanation: a8=Q turns your humble pawn into a queen. Now the win is easy. Time to Grind.

lessons.title: Pawn Structures
lessons.description: Pawns are the soul of chess — learn to read the structure.

steps.explanation: Pawn chains point in a direction — attack the base of the chain. Isolated, doubled, and backward pawns are long-term weaknesses.
The side your pawns point toward is the side you attack. Space from a pawn chain tells you where your plan lives.

lessons.title: How to Calculate Moves
lessons.description: Think ahead without getting lost. Calculate like a machine.

steps.explanation: Look at checks, captures and threats. Calculate the most forcing move to the end before considering quiet options.

steps.prompt: Calculate the forcing move that ends it (Ra8#).
steps.explanation: The most forcing move — a check that is also mate — ends the game instantly. Always calculate checks first. Checkmate. GG.

tactics.explanation: Nf6+ forks the king and queen. The king moves, then Nxd5 wins the queen.
The queen is pinned to the king by the g1 rook, so it can't run. Grab it with hxg5. Clean Move 🔥
Rh8+ skewers the king to the queen. When the king steps aside, Rxb8 wins the queen.
Nf5+ discovers check from the bishop and also attacks the queen. After the king moves, Nxd6 wins.
Qe4+ attacks the king and the rook simultaneously. The king moves, then Qxh4 wins the rook.
Qb8+ forces the queen to block on the back rank, where you capture it. Deflect the defender and win the queen.
Qg8+!! decoys the rook: after Rxg8, Nf7# is a smothered mate. The king can't take the queen (the knight guards g8).
Qxh7# removes the king's last shield. The queen is protected by the g5 knight, so it's checkmate. GG.
Your knight is attacked, but don't retreat! Nf6+ is the in-between move — it checks the king and forks the queen. After the king moves, Nxd5 wins the queen.
Ra8# — the king is trapped behind its own pawns. Checkmate on the back rank. GG.
Nf7# — the king is smothered by its own rook and pawns and can't escape the knight's check. Checkmate. GG.
Rh7# — the knight guards g8 and h7's approach while the rook mates. The classic Arabian mate.
